meta.title: Ukrainian C1 Advanced
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Ukrainian → English (see the Ukrainian, recall the meaning) and English → Ukrainian (see an English meaning, recall the Ukrainian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words for an advanced learner, aligned to C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognise implicit meaning' — a learner here is able to express ideas fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions, to use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes, and to produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Ukraine certifies proficiency in the language but publishes no graded word list, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 274 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — politics, power and the state, law and justice, the economy and finance, science and research, philosophy and belief, language, literature and style, the arts and taste, the mind, emotion and behaviour, society and how it changes, the land and the planet, the small words of nuance, and the verbs of arguing, deciding and shading a meaning — and the other 1226 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Ukrainian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Cyrillic with its stress marked (кни́га, роблю́), because Ukrainian stress can fall on any syllable and move as the word changes, and nothing else shows it; there is no transliteration, and the Ukrainian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters. The 774 nouns show their gender, their genitive and their plural; the 403 verbs show their aspect, imperfective or perfective, with the other verb of the pair beside them, their я and він forms and their past; and behind the All forms fold every noun's seven cases and every verb's tenses by person. Real example sentences come with 1216 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 920 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender, aspect, stress and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
